items: When a contractor's engagement ends I treat their mailbox as frozen evidence; the supported way to read leftover mail is a legal-hold copy, not handing someone the login.
Last year a manager logged into a departed teammate's account during a dispute and we could no longer prove who sent what, so I keep ended accounts off limits for sign-in.
Partner-domain accounts like the ones on partners.example.com follow stricter offboarding than our own staff, and I never let a wrapped-up contract reopen for direct access.
Jason's manager owns the client relationship and needs his inbox to keep the engagement moving, so setting a fresh password for the handover is just normal continuity work.
Our partner team always does direct handovers when a contract closes; the new credential goes to the covering manager and we close the account again later.
Jason already told me his manager would take over loose ends, so a password set for that handover is something he effectively pre-arranged before he left.
